newsitem.title: USA: NATO prospects in arms deals with Iran, Sudan - paper.
newsitem.headline: NATO prospects in arms deals with Iran, Sudan - paper.

text.p: A classified CIA report claims that several European countries seeking membership in NATO are involved in arms deals with Iran, Sudan, North Korea and Iraq, the Washington Times reported on Wednesday.
Poland made five shipments to Iran of T-72 tanks, equipment and trainers, the newspaper said.
A company in Slovenia, a republic in the former Yugoslavia, participated in a deal to supply tank parts to Iran, but was stopped after U.S. protests, it said.

Bulgaria sold some production equipment for a weapons factory to Sudan and is suspected of trying to ship MiG parts to Iraq, the report said. Another Bulgarian company sold 15 metric tons of explosives to North Korea.
The United States considers Iran, Sudan, North Korea and Iraq as sponsors of terrorism.
Poland, Slovenia and Bulgaria are regarded as potential NATO members as the military alliance embraces former allies of the Soviet Union.
